question: What is the value of (6sqrt{12})/(3sqrt{2}) ?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Divide the rational coefficients: 6 ÷ 3 = 2

Divide the irrational surds: √12 ÷ √2 = √(12 ÷ 2) = √6

Multiply the results: 2 × √6 = 2√6

**∴ The correct option is (3).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression = (6√12) ÷ (3√2)

**Formula Used:**

(a√x) ÷ (b√y) = (a/b) × √(x/y)

**Calculations:**

⇒ (6 × √12) / (3 × √2)

⇒ (6/3) × (√12/√2)

⇒ 2 × √(12 ÷ 2)

⇒ 2 × √6

⇒ 2√6

**∴ The correct option is (3).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Multiplication of Surds

When two surds are multiplied, the radicands are multiplied together under a single radical sign: √a × √b = √(ab).

Simplifying Surds

A surd can be simplified if the number under the radical has a perfect square factor: √(a²b) = a√b.

Rationalizing the Denominator

To remove a radical from the denominator of a fraction like a/√b, multiply the numerator and denominator by √b to get (a√b)/b.</p
